attempted_axis: Three distinct source spellings of one indirect vtable call, trying to make MWCC resolve the vtable pointer at point of use in r12 (as the target does) instead of hoisting it early into the volatile r4.

attributes.law_screen: claim.law.point-of-use-single-use-pointer-delay SCREENED and NOT applicable in its stated form: it governs a local declared with an initializer at function entry whose sole read is later, whereas this callee is already an inline subexpression with no named local. Its spirit (resolve at point of use) motivated axes 1-3, all negative. claim.law.reload-vs-cache-liveness SCREENED - no member-pointer cache across calls is involved. claim.law.address-cse-over-calls-outranks-member-displacement-form SCREENED - the target and our build agree on the base register (r30) and displacement (368), so no address-spelling lever applies. claim.law.EN-ops-multiset-cannot-classify-a-residual-run-slotdiff-first APPLIED: fndiff reports insns 38/38 with multiset 0t (IDENTICAL), so the residual is confirmed pure reorder plus one recolor.
attributes.probed_form: Baseline (retained): `(*(MovieCloseVTable**)(self + offsetof(MovieState, decoderVtable)))->close(self + 336);`  AXIS 1, flatten the callee to an anonymous double-load: `(*(void (**)(u8*))(*(u8**)(self + offsetof(MovieState, decoderVtable)) + 28))(self + 336);` -> NEUTRAL.  AXIS 2, make the vtable load DEPEND on the object pointer so the argument must be computed first: `{ register u8* dec = self + 336; (*(MovieCloseVTable**)(dec + 32))->close(dec); }` -> NEUTRAL (MWCC refolds dec+32 back to 368(r30)).  AXIS 3, pin the load at point of use with a volatile read: `(*(MovieCloseVTable* volatile*)(self + offsetof(MovieState, decoderVtable)))->close(self + 336);` -> NEUTRAL.
attributes.residual: NAMED MECHANISM, do-not-retry on callee-expression shape. Exactly 3 instructions differ, as a pure reorder plus one recolor. Target: `addi r3,r30,336 / lwz r12,368(r30) / lwz r12,28(r12)` - the argument is materialised FIRST, then the vtable chain resolves through r12 twice, which is CodeWarrior's canonical virtual-call sequence with `this` in r3. Ours: `lwz r4,368(r30) / addi r3,r30,336 / lwz r12,28(r4)` - the independent vtable load is hoisted ahead of the argument into the free volatile r4. The two loads are independent of the argument, so MWCC's scheduler is free to order them either way and no source spelling of a FREE function-pointer call expresses the constraint; only a genuine C++ virtual call emits the canned two-step r12 chain. Reaching it would require declaring the class with real `virtual` members, which this TU deliberately avoids (claim.law.destructor-throw-spec-adds-a-second-unexpected-island step 3) because a virtual spelling emits a `__vt__` object into a TU whose split owns no .data. NOTE the vtable offset is decisive evidence and is worth keeping: 28 = slot5 of __vt__7VQCodec = fn_800D8784, per claim.symbol-naming-movieplayer-cpp-class-map v4's slot map, so this call is `decoder->slot5(self + 336)` and the TU's invented `close` name is consistent with it.
